08b_1_scale_factors.png: The scale factors of the author's corrected metric along the prescribed deflating history $a_4 = A H x_4$, $b_4 = b_4(0)\,e^{4AHx_4/3}$ ($A = H = 1$, $b_4(0) = 1$) against the time $x_4$ in units of $1/m$, on a logarithmic vertical axis, at the fold $y = 0$ (solid) and at $y = -1$ (dashed). Blue: 3-space, $e^{a_4}$, a rising straight line (exponential inflation, $e^{x_4}$), the same at every hidden position. Green: the hidden direction, $e^{-a_4}b_4^{1/2}$ per unit of $y$, and red: the extra times, $e^{-a_4}b_4^{1/2}e^{Hy}$; both fall like $e^{-x_4/3}$ (the hidden block deflates as one; at $y = 0$ the red line lies on the green one). Black: the 7-volume factor per unit of the coordinates $x_1, x_2, x_3, y, x_5, x_6, x_7$, $e^{-a_4}b_4^2e^{3Hy}$, which grows like $e^{5x_4/3}$.
08b_2_frame_momenta.png: Left: the frame momenta of one wave with coordinate wave numbers $q_1 = q_5 = 0.1$ and the local hidden wave number $q_y = 0.05$ at $y = 0$ against the time $x_4$, on a logarithmic axis in units of $m$, along the history $a_4 = x_4$, $b_4 = e^{4x_4/3}$: the extra-time momentum $k_{(5)} = q_5e^{x_4/3}$ and the hidden momentum $k_{(0)} = q_ye^{x_4/3}$ grow at the same rate (the hidden block deflates as one), the space momentum $k_{(1)} = q_1e^{-a_4}$ shrinks (3-space inflates); dotted: the mass $m = 1$. Right: the local $E^2$ of five waves without hidden momentum along the history; each curve crosses zero once, at its onset time (black dot), and stays negative: the wave stops oscillating and starts to grow. The dashed wave has also $q_1 = 1$: its $E^2$ starts higher, but the space term dies away like $e^{-2a_4}$ and its onset is almost that of the same wave with $q_1 = 0$.
08b_3_onset_times.png: Left: the onset time $x_4^\ast$ at which a wave with coordinate wave number $q_5$ along the extra time $x_5$ and no hidden momentum starts to grow, against $q_5$ from $10^{-4}$ to $1$ (logarithmic axis), along the history $a_4 = x_4$, $b_4 = e^{4x_4/3}$ with $m = H = 1$, at the hidden positions $y = 0$ (the fold), $y = -1$ and $y = -3$ (the tip cutoff of the Kohn-Sham record), and for a wave with $q_1 = 1$. Every curve is finite and rises only like $3\ln(1/q_5)$; a negative onset time means growth already at $x_4 = 0$. Right: the local $E^2$ of a wave with $q_5 = 0.1$ at $y = 0$ and the hidden wave numbers $q_y = 0, 0.05, 0.08$ (solid; $D > 0$, onsets at the black dots), $q_y = 0.1$ (dashed; $D = 0$, $E^2 = 1$ at every time) and $q_y = 0.12$ (dotted; $D < 0$): because the hidden direction deflates with the extra times, a large enough hidden momentum keeps the wave oscillating for ever.
08b_4_growth_along_history.png: The natural logarithm of the size $u^\dagger u$ of a wave with coordinate wave number $q_5 = 0.05$ (blue) and $q_5 = 0.1$ (orange) along the extra time $x_5$ and no hidden momentum, solved with RK4 in the local-frame model along the prescribed deflating history $a_4 = x_4$, $b_4 = e^{4x_4/3}$ ($m = H = 1$, $y = 0$), against the time $x_4$ in units of $1/m$. Before the onset (dotted vertical lines, $x_4^\ast = 3\ln 20$ and $3\ln 10$) the wave oscillates and its size grows only slowly, to about 2 at the onset (the mode matrix is not Hermitian); after the onset it grows faster and faster, by about 48 powers of ten in nine time units, following the WKB curve $2W$ (black dashed, matched 4.5 units after the onset).
08b_5_rate_and_krein.png: Left: the growth rate $d\ln(u^\dagger u)/dx_4$ of the wave with $q_5 = 0.05$ against the time $x_4$ (units of $1/m$ and $m$), computed from the RK4 solution (blue), with the leading WKB rate $2\kappa$ (black dashed) and the first-order rate $2\kappa - \delta m^2/\kappa^2$ with $\delta = 1/3$ (red dotted); before the onset the rate stays below 1, after it the rate itself grows exponentially, so the growth is faster than any exponential, and far from the onset the first-order rate is accurate. Right: the change of the Krein form $u^\dagger Bu$ divided by $\max(u^\dagger u, 1)$, on a logarithmic axis (exact zeros are drawn at $10^{-18}$); it stays at the level of rounding errors, far below $10^{-9}$.
